checks.item: 'Uses the GPU if Docker can reach it' as shipped
checks.evidence: Cannot be shown to work, and the shipped files cannot do it. (1) docker-compose.yml speech service has no GPU reservation (no deploy.resources.reservations.devices / gpus), and build defaults to a CPU-only ubuntu:24.04 image (GGML_CUDA=OFF), so compose never uses the GPU. (2) The documented GPU recipe in the Dockerfile header uses nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-*-ubuntu22.04, but the runtime stage hard-codes apt packages libgrpc++1.51t64 and libprotobuf32t64, which exist only on Ubuntu 24.04; on 22.04 apt-cache shows libgrpc++1 1.30.2 and libprotobuf23 instead, so that build would fail at apt-get install. nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-*-ubuntu24.04 does not exist (manifest inspect: missing; 12.6.2 ubuntu24.04 exists). Also the gRPC 1.30 on 22.04 may not match the code assumptions. (3) The GPU path was never built or run.

failures: GPU requirement not met as shipped. Dockerfile runtime stage (apt-get install libgrpc++1.51t64 libprotobuf32t64) is Ubuntu 24.04 only, but the documented GPU build args in the Dockerfile header use ubuntu22.04 CUDA images, so that recipe fails; no ubuntu24.04 tag exists for CUDA 12.4.1. docker-compose.yml's speech service has no GPU device reservation, so 'docker compose up' cannot reach a GPU. Reproduce: docker run --rm ubuntu:22.04 apt-cache policy libgrpc++1.51t64 (no candidate), docker manifest inspect nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-devel-ubuntu24.04 (missing). Fix: choose a CUDA base tag that exists for the same Ubuntu release as the package names (e.g. 12.6.2 on 24.04), add a GPU option to compose (override file or device reservation), and make backend reporting reflect the device actually used. GPU verification needs one GPU turn: build with the CUDA bases and GGML_CUDA=ON, run with --gpus all, confirm x-compute-backend starts with gpu: and the fixture still transcribes. The CPU path needs no GPU turn.
notes: CPU path is solid and ctest gating is verified. What I could not check: any CUDA build, GPU detection (detect_backend lists registered GGML GPU devices, not the one whisper actually used; if whisper falls back it could still say gpu), --gpus behavior on a machine without CUDA. whisper.cpp pinned by tag, not commit hash. Segments only appear after an utterance ends (no partials). Wrong-format audio is not rejected, only yields nothing.
